hypotheses.claim: Under the 500 ms anytime LNS budget, on n=100 / uniform / eccentric-depot / loose-capacity CVRP instances the current fixed-size Worst-Cost removal wastes iterations on marginally-improving small neighborhoods and never escapes local optima within the deadline. A size-scaled hybrid destroy score (worst-cost z-score + Shaw relatedness to the route centroid, with |R| growing as ~sqrt(n) and time-decayed) will increase the count of accepted improving moves per unit time and yield >=1% lower mean objective on n=100 instances without regressing small-n (<=50) instances beyond 0.5%, since small-n keeps a near-fixed small removal set.

next_search_advice.direction: Evolve the `score_ruin_nodes` destruction-priority hook toward a size-aware hybrid: combine normalized worst-cost removal (high detour saving) with Shaw relatedness to the last-depot/route-centroid, and scale the per-iteration ruin fraction with instance size (larger n=100 gets a modestly larger removal set |R| ramping from ~4 to ~12 nodes) while keeping Regret-2 recreate and Record-to-Record acceptance untouched. Focus the reward shaping on the weakest regimes: n=100, uniform spatial, eccentric depot, uniform demand, loose capacity — where the archive shows the largest negative VBS gap (exhausted instances, ~-20% rel gap).
